items.headline: Localized UX drove fintech landing page for Philippine users
items.background: Fintech products in Southeast Asia often fail to convert because they apply Western design conventions to markets with distinct payment infrastructure, trust signals, and financial literacy levels. This case study addresses that gap for the Philippine market.
keyFindings: Localized payment integrations were treated as a core UX decision, not a dev handoff afterthought
Transparent data architecture — showing users how yields are calculated — was used as a primary trust mechanism
High-converting landing pages in this market required explicit democratization framing to address skepticism around digital assets
items.implications: Relevant to product designers working on fintech in emerging markets: conversion optimization here is less about CTA placement and more about legibility of financial mechanisms and payment familiarity. Don't port Western fintech patterns wholesale.

items.headline: Wealth management UX built for Philippine multi-currency complexity
items.background: Wealth management portals typically target high-net-worth users in Western markets, but growing middle-class investor segments in Southeast Asia need tools that handle multi-currency flows and institutional trust signals in locally relevant ways.
keyFindings: Multi-currency data flows were designed as a UX architecture problem, not just a backend concern
Institutional trust markers — visual and structural cues borrowed from established finance — were deliberately embedded in the UI
The portal targeted complexity reduction as its core UX goal, not feature completeness
items.implications: For product teams building financial tools in APAC: trust is communicated through structural clarity and familiar institutional cues, not just brand polish. Information architecture decisions here directly affect perceived credibility.

items.headline: AI accounting dashboards need less data, more explanation
items.background: As AI handles more back-office work like data ingestion and categorization, designers are left with a UI problem: what does a dashboard show when the AI has already done most of the work? Traditional data-dense dashboards may be the wrong pattern.
keyFindings: When AI completes the primary task, the dashboard's job shifts from enabling action to communicating confidence and status
Showing less data — not more — tested better for comprehension in an AI accounting ingestion screen
Explaining what the AI did and why matters more to users than showing the full output
items.implications: Designers building AI-assisted products should audit whether their dashboards are still optimized for human-driven workflows. If the AI is doing the work, users need legibility and trust signals, not raw data access.

items.headline: Stop shipping PNGs: designers should hand off tokens, not images
items.background: The gap between design files and production code remains a persistent source of rework and miscommunication on product teams. Static image exports in particular create ambiguity around spacing, states, and behavior that slows engineering.
keyFindings: PNG handoffs force developers to make interpretive decisions that designers intended to specify
Structured Figma files with named components, constraints, and annotated states reduce implementation errors
The author frames this as a workflow cost problem — lost time, not just lost quality
items.implications: Applies most directly to small-to-mid product teams without dedicated design engineers. Moving to component-based handoffs with documented states is a process change, not just a tool change — it requires alignment on what 'done' means in design.

items.headline: IIT Bombay's interaction design program: what it covers
items.background: Jaro Education published a curriculum overview for IIT Bombay's executive postgraduate diploma in interaction design, targeting working professionals looking to formalize UX skills.
keyFindings: The program covers interaction design principles, prototyping, and user research methods
It is structured as an executive PGD, targeting mid-career professionals rather than entry-level candidates
IIT Bombay's institutional credibility is positioned as a key differentiator in the Indian design education market
items.implications: Useful context for practitioners in India evaluating formal credentialing options. Content appears to be promotional rather than independently reviewed — verify curriculum depth before enrolling.
